name: shaders-smaa (glsl-smaa, wgsl-smaa)
role: SMAA antialiasing passes as GLSL and WGSL shader strings for raw WebGL and WebGPU renderers
summary: glsl-smaa 4.0.0 ships the SMAA edges, weights and blend shaders and the reference lookup textures as ES module strings; wgsl-smaa 1.0.0 is the WGSL port. You wire three framebuffer passes yourself in any raw WebGL renderer. Its strength is SMAA outside a Three.js composer. 1x mode is spatial only, so each frame depends only on its input and seeks cleanly; T2x is history-dependent.
use_when: Aliased edges in a raw WebGL, regl, twgl or ogl scene with no antialiasing pass
Over postprocessing's SMAA when the scene does not use a Three.js composer
Post-process antialiasing where MSAA is unavailable, such as on a render-to-texture target
avoid_when: A Three.js scene: postprocessing or react-three-postprocessing bring SMAA with a composer
Alpha-keyed output: edge detection reads colour, and alpha is untested here
Seek-driven capture with T2x: it blends the previous frame, so use 1x
notes: 2026-11-27: wgsl-smaa 1.0.0 (WebGPU) is untested; the fixture covers glsl-smaa only. Quality against postprocessing's SMAA was not compared pixel for pixel.
2026-11-27: The README warns of a flipped y sign in WebGL T2x jitter and that alpha is overwritten when reprojection is on; neither was exercised.

assessment.rationale: glsl-smaa 4.0.0 and wgsl-smaa 1.0.0 published 2026-09-24; MIT; the only catalogue route to SMAA outside a Three.js composer. Shaders only: the caller writes the pass wiring. No upstream tests against the reference are described.

evidence.result: 90 frames at 1280x720; shuffled hashes equal sequential; frame 45 unique colours 4 aliased half vs 455 SMAA half, alpha min 1. glsl-smaa 4.0.0, Playwright 1.64.1, Chromium 156.0.8078.4, Node 22.19.0, WebGL1; 4x crop inspected: staircases gone, geometry intact.
evidence.scope: SMAA 1x (HIGH, luma edges) on an opaque raw WebGL1 scene, macOS arm64 Chromium; not wgsl-smaa, T2x, alpha, depth edges, WebGL2 or comparison with postprocessing.
